title: MZ Plugin that lets you change between soundtrack versions like Final Fantasy Pixel Remasters

posts.author: james5272
posts.body:
Hey there,
Some months ago, I wrote synth music with live drums with the idea it would be used in my 2nd game. I have since converted it to 8-bit and am currently using the 8-bit versions as the music in my game. However, I would also like to have the synth with live drums music in my game, and let the player choose which soundtrack (8-bit or synth) is being used. The Final Fantasy Pixel Remasters do this, you can choose the original system's soundtracks, or the modern live instrument ones.
Is there a way to do this in RPG Maker MZ?

posts.author: DrFreeman
posts.body:
The basic idea is you want a switch between 8-bit soundtrack or Synth soundtrack. For most maps you could do it pretty easily with a switch or switches, but for the combat, that would require a plugin.
This is a free option:
https://castiger.itch.io/kotc-optimized-dynamic-music-system-rpg-maker-mv-mz
. It would require a bit more configuring per situation.
This plugin is $9, but it sounds like it will do exactly what you want:
https://heroicjay.itch.io/soundtrack-manager-for-rpg-maker-mv
.
There are a couple other options, but you might need to get creative with them. They were designed more for jukebox options.
Caspergaming has his
Jukebox plugin
.
Undermax has a
Media Player plugin
.
Tome's
Custom Audio loops plugin
.
If you're feeling that you want it to be exactly how you want it then this is the Mozilla link on
how to play audio
with HTML5 + JS. You would just want to add a variable to control your soundtrack selection. There is also a post on how to
make plugins here
.
Maybe someone else on the forums might have an easier idea than me?

thats the bigger issue and is the cause of the other problem.
before a sound file is buffered, the plugin checks to see if the file exists. if it doesnt, it assumes that youre trying to load a suffixed file and chops off the last few characters. the sound file its looking for would actually be "James" followed by some 6 characters. itd be either your ok, buzzer, cancel, or cursor sound effect. the reason the plugin does it is so that it can make the game not give you an error for not having suffixed versions of every sound file.
When you encrypt the project, the extension the plugin expects changes and it messes with what the plugin does to search for the files. unfortunately it doesnt seem to be the case that making it look for the updated extension seems to work either... somehow. the only recourse i could think of besides not encrypting the audio files would be to remove the part of the plugin that checks to see if the files exist and then have you make suffixed files for each sound file in the project
